mechaber/1:main: Laws of bedikat chametz. Containing 11 seifim. Bedikat chametz must be by candlelight, not moonlight. If one did not check on the night of the 14th, when checking on the day of the 14th one should not check by sunlight but by candlelight. However, for a portico whose light is great, if one checked by sunlight it suffices; and the same applies to checking opposite the skylight in a room.
mechaber/2:main: One does not check by torchlight but by candlelight — not with a tallow candle, nor of fat, nor of oil, but with a wax candle. {Rama: And this is when it is a single candle; but two candles together, even braided ones, have the law of a torch (Maharil in the name of the Agudah).}
mechaber/3:main: One checks every place where there is concern that chametz was brought in; therefore all rooms of the house and attics require checking, for sometimes a person enters with bread in his hand. But wine cellars where bread is not suspected, and likewise a barn and the like, do not require checking.
mechaber/4:main: Holes of the house and projecting cornices from the walls that are not very high nor very low require checking. But those too high for a person's hand to reach, and those less than three handbreadths low, do not require checking.
mechaber/5:main: The roof of a lean-to or tower whose roofs are slanted — since for that reason their roofs are unfit for any use — do not require checking even if they are inside the house.
mechaber/6:main: A cattle shed does not require checking, for if there was chametz there the animals would eat it. Likewise a chicken coop does not require checking, for if there was chametz there the chickens would eat it. Likewise the middle of a courtyard does not require checking, for if there was chametz there the ravens and other birds found there would eat it. This is regarding possible chametz; but for definite chametz, no. {Rama: But below siman 445 seif 3 it is explained that it is permitted to discard chametz where birds are found — certainly one need not remove even definite chametz from there before its prohibition time.}
mechaber/7:main: For a hole between one Jew and another, each checks as far as his hand reaches, and the rest he nullifies in his heart, which suffices. But between a Jew and a non-Jew one need not check at all, lest the non-Jew say "He is doing sorcery against me" and this leads to danger.
mechaber/8:main: A wall that was used with chametz in its holes, and it collapsed and became a mound — even if not three handbreadths high, enough for a dog to dig — one need not check underneath, since there is danger of scorpions found in mounds; we are concerned that after he finishes his checking, no longer engaged in a mitzvah, he may search there for a lost needle and come to danger. This is in general; but if it is known there is chametz under a mound less than three handbreadths high, he must remove it with a hoe and shovel in a manner without danger. If it is three handbreadths high or more, he nullifies it in his heart, which suffices.
mechaber/9:main: A cellar where they arrange rows of barrels one next to another until it is full, then arrange more rows on top of the lower ones up to the beam — one need only check the top row and another below it, meaning a row across the width of the cellar, not the entire area of the cellar, but the top row visible from the beam and the entrance, and another below it.
mechaber/10:main: Synagogues and study halls require checking, because children bring chametz into them.
mechaber/11:main: One who cleans his room on the 13th of Nisan intending to check for chametz and burn it, being careful not to bring more chametz in, must still check on the night of the 14th. {Rama: And everyone must clean his rooms before checking (Mordechai at the beginning of Pesachim). Pockets or sleeves of garments where chametz is sometimes placed require checking (Mahari Weil).}
turei-zahav/1:א: And if he passed. In Tur it is written: even if one checks by day — meaning not only that l'chatchila one should not rely to check by sunlight, i.e. wait for daylight, but even if he already passed and must check by day, nevertheless he needs a candle; and so Beit Yosef, and this is correct. And since he did not find to write a novelty except for the 14th and not the 13th, it implies checking on the 13th does not help since the Sages fixed the time for the night of the 14th — it is as one who checks a long time before Pesach; and so Beit Yosef concludes for halacha.
turei-zahav/1:ב: And a portico whose light is great. Beit Yosef wrote: when checking on that day — it appears his intent is that this law of a portico also applies when one does the entire checking on the 14th, e.g. he passed and did not check at night; but l'chatchila he should also check the portico at night by candlelight. Rashi implies even l'chatchila he need not use candlelight but by day; and so Rif, and the conclusion of Mahari Weil and most poskim is that it is specifically b'dieved.
turei-zahav/2:_: One does not check by torchlight. See Tur for the reason — it appears here it is forbidden l'chatchila but not to invalidate b'dieved, unlike sunlight and moonlight which are not called checking at all and do not help even b'dieved; and so Tur's language implies at the beginning: for sunlight and moonlight one must use candlelight, which teaches even b'dieved; but for a torch he wrote "one does not check," implying l'chatchila not, but b'dieved it is also called checking. Therefore what he wrote afterward — "therefore Ashkenazim practice only with a wax candle" — implies custom; and since he spoke regarding torch law, it follows they are comparable: although the baraita states both in one clause "one does not check by sunlight nor by torch because candlelight is good for checking," nevertheless from "because candlelight is good" it implies it is good but not to invalidate; and automatically for what the baraita first said "one does not check by sunlight" it refers even b'dieved; and what he said in another clause "nor by torch" means l'chatchila, and on that alone he said at the end "because candlelight is good for checking" — from this language it is proven l'chatchila but not to invalidate, as I wrote.
turei-zahav/4:_: That are not very high. Tur wrote, and in Yerushalmi they consider high above ten handbreadths; or alternatively, etc. — it appears therefore Tur argues because in our Gemara it says until his hand reaches, implying the opposite, as I wrote.
turei-zahav/6:_: But below siman 445. It appears to resolve: there it refers to one who throws into the city street so ravens will eat — therefore permitted; but here it refers to chametz found in a courtyard, and in this case certainly it is not correct — see siman 445.
turei-zahav/7:_: And between a Jew and a non-Jew. It would appear to say that even for definite chametz one need not check because of danger; and although regarding a mound definite chametz must be removed with a hoe and shovel — there is different, for there he can do so without danger, unlike here where he cannot act without danger; but in truth here too definite chametz requires checking — by day, as proven in the Gemara which asks "how did he use it" and answers "when he used it by day in light" — he does not consider it, as I wrote.
turei-zahav/8:א: He may search for a needle. Rishon L'Tzion wrote: Rashi explained "that it was lost to him" before the checking — it appears his intent is not to say a needle was lost during checking when his mind was diverted by checking and that caused harm — for then the difficulty returns to its place: agents of a mitzvah are not harmed, and how can one say harm came from checking; rather it refers to one already lost before checking, but after checking he will immediately search for the needle while the checking candle is still in his hand — although here too one could say agents of a mitzvah, nevertheless since the loss already preceded him and checking did not cause the main harm, since he could search whenever he wished — with this the difficulties of Beit Yosef on the poskim who omitted the distinction between general and known cases are resolved, as that distinction is necessary per the first resolution in the Gemara regarding scorpion danger; because Tosafot's difficulty — that regarding a mound it implies if a dog can dig after him it is not as concealed and requires saying it refers to definite chametz — but in truth Ramban does not hold the first resolution regarding scorpion danger, because it was difficult for him: even if checking caused searching for a needle even if already lost beforehand, nevertheless he is within agents of a mitzvah, etc. Therefore he resolves regarding non-Jewish danger where harm is common — therefore Tosafot's difficulty has no place; and one can say even for possible chametz one may check with scorpion danger, and here it refers to non-Jewish danger; and poskim who omitted the distinction hold like Ramban, as I wrote.
turei-zahav/8:ב: He nullifies in his heart and it suffices. So in the Gemara daf 30 in the mishnah: chametz that fell on him from a collapse — R' Chisda says he must nullify it; Rashi explained lest he open the mound on the festival and be found transgressing; Semak wrote he must nullify because of "you shall not hide" — implying even where he will not open the mound on the festival he must nullify, otherwise he transgresses "you shall not hide," i.e. the prohibition applies even if he hides until after Pesach; Rashi does not hold so, since he does not hide with his hands he does not transgress. It is simple to me that Shulchan Aruch's words that one need not check because of scorpion danger is also in this way that he must nullify in his heart if there is chametz there for this reason; and from this the baraita is explained that they do not obligate putting hands into holes because of danger — meaning with hands there is no obligation, but nullification in the heart is required, as I wrote. Hagahot Alfasi in the name of Riaz: if it has height of three handbreadths, since he did not transgress "it shall not be seen," it is permitted in eating after Pesach with no concern for trickery since it fell from a collapse — end. It appears there is a distinction: if there was first a wall there and it fell, certainly he will clear the collapse to repair the wall, somewhat like hiding in pits; but if a collapse of stones fell on him in a way with no expectation of clearing, then after Pesach it is permitted if he nullified. On what is written regarding less than three handbreadths that he must remove — one could ask why not say a dog will eat it as written regarding ravens, that regarding ravens too it is forbidden when in his possession — see siman 445 seif 3.
baer-heitev/1:א: By candlelight. On the night of the 14th; and even if he checked on the 13th by candlelight he must return and check on the night of the 14th. However, if he checked on the night of the 13th and was very careful not to bring more chametz, he need not check again — Kaf HaChayyim, see there, Levush, and Bach wrote that even if he checked on the night of the 13th he must return on the night of the 14th; Kaf HaChayyim concluded: if he wishes to be stringent on himself, at least he should not bless then lest he enter a doubtful blessing situation, but he may return and use chametz there and then bless and check.
baer-heitev/1:ב: Skylight. Meaning a window in the roof (see chapter 5 of Beitzah mishnah 1 and chapter 10 of Ohalot). If there is a glass partition there, it is forbidden to check opposite it — Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/2:_: The torch. Even b'dieved it does not help; but a tallow or fat candle helps b'dieved. An oil candle has the law of a torch; if he has no wax candle he checks with oil; if he has no oil he checks l'chatchila with tallow — one does not check with wood called kiyin — Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/3:_: That bread is not suspected. If bread is suspected and he has a fixed practice to take at once what he needs for a meal, no checking is required — Magen Avraham. Maharil (Mahari Weil) wrote in a responsum: where they eat there all year, one should check under the benches, for it is impossible chametz did not fall there — it is clear chametz (if there are no chickens there). One should not throw grain to chickens in a damp place thirty days before Pesach — Maharil.
baer-heitev/4:_: Less than three handbreadths. If children are found there, checking is required.
baer-heitev/6:_: Explained. See there Taz and Magen Avraham and Kaf HaChayyim what they resolved.
baer-heitev/7:_: Checking at all. Nevertheless by day he checks by daylight as he used the place — so Magen Avraham, Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/8:א: Scorpion. Specifically where scorpions are found; and see siman 104 seif 2 that implies a snake's harm is not certain and checking is required — Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/8:ב: He nullifies it. Acharonim wrote he may eat it after Pesach since he did not transgress "it shall not be seen," and there is no concern for trickery since it fell from a collapse. Bach left this in doubt; Taz also divides this law; Magen Avraham wrote in the name of Rashba's responsum that Rav Hai forbids, and if he did not nullify it and it is after prohibition time he must clear the mound to destroy the chametz since it is no longer in his power to nullify — Acharonim; Magen Avraham wrote: if a large mound fell on him that he cannot open and it is lost from him and everyone, it is permitted even without nullifying, for we do not call it "yours."
baer-heitev/10:_: Checking. Meaning on the night of the 14th — Magen Avraham; and it appears if he passed and did not check on the night of the 14th, he checks even l'chatchila on the 14th by sunlight like a portico whose light is also great. I have not seen people careful about this to check the synagogue — sweeping suffices; one should warn the shamashim of the synagogue about this, and so Maharil. He also wrote some places announce after checking the synagogue that children should not come there again with chametz.
baer-heitev/11:א: On the 13th. Specifically by day; but if he checked on the night of the 13th he need not return on the night of the 14th, as in s.k. 1.
baer-heitev/11:ב: On the night of the 14th. A portico: if he checked on the 13th by sunlight he has fulfilled; nevertheless at least one room should be checked at night — Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/11:ג: That they sometimes place chametz in them. One whose practice is not so need not check — Darkei Moshe, Magen Avraham; Kaf HaChayyim is stringent — see there.
magen-avraham/1:א: And if he passed. But l'chatchila it is forbidden to check by day, even in a dark house, by candlelight.
magen-avraham/1:ב: And a portico. Meaning built on pillars and has no wall.
magen-avraham/1:ג: If he checked. The Gemara states that l'chatchila they check a portico by sunlight — it must refer when checking on the 14th; but l'chatchila he must check on the night of the 14th by candlelight, as this siman states; therefore he wrote b'dieved language — so there is no dispute, as Ri'az and most hold, unlike Bach.
magen-avraham/1:ד: Opposite a skylight. Meaning a window in the roof; so in mishnah chapter 1 of Ohalot and chapter 5 of Beitzah; therefore Ri'az wrote it is forbidden to check opposite the window — window means in the wall; and Beit Yosef's view is that even opposite a window in the wall is permitted, and so most hold in Rambam: holes and cracks in the house — those opposite the skylight are checked by daylight, etc. — implying even if the sun does not shine; and it appears for a window with a glass partition all forbid checking opposite it.
magen-avraham/2:א: And not by candle. That he separated torch and tallow candle and did not write them in one clause — because a torch appears in the Gemara to forbid, and there are many reasons permitting putting it into holes and cracks lest he burn the house, and also because its light is behind him and flickers; if so, even b'dieved he must return and check. But a tallow candle — they were stringent that it is permitted lest it drip on vessels and garments; b'dieved he has fulfilled. Oil candle has the law of a torch, fearing to put it into holes lest oil spill. You might ask: wax too — one fears dripping on garments; one may say it can be fixed with a full spoon of coals.
magen-avraham/2:ב: Even braided. This language is not in Maharil — what does "even" mean, etc.; certainly if not braided it is permitted since each can be brought to holes; it appears the intent is: it is obvious if glued together and not braided it is like a torch; but even if braided, one might think it is like one candle — he teaches otherwise.
magen-avraham/3:_: That bread is not suspected. Wine cellars where bread is suspected and he has a fixed practice to take at once what he needs for a meal — no checking, for they are not accustomed to enter with bread.
magen-avraham/4:_: Less than three handbreadths. If children are found, checking is required — Ra'avad, Beit Yosef.
magen-avraham/6:א: Chicken coop. Likewise the floor of the house where chickens are found — no checking (Beit Yosef, Ri'az, Rashba); and Mahari Weil wrote one must sweep under the beds because sometimes chametz is dragged there in chickens' mouths or another reason — end; it appears his intent: a small piece chickens eat, but we fear a large piece remains that chickens cannot eat — therefore sweeping suffices without checking. And where they eat all year and there are no chickens, check under benches — impossible chametz did not fall — it is like clear chametz in a pit (Mahari Weil).
magen-avraham/6:ב: But below. If so, here in Shulchan Aruch it also refers after prohibition time; Bach wrote below: in a courtyard where many participate it is like an ownerless courtyard — even if chametz remains he does not transgress; but in his own courtyard, if there was definite chametz, checking is required, for doubt does not remove certainty, as siman 438; so in the Gemara daf 100, etc.; for this reason checking is required; in a room where they regularly eat, even if chickens are there, it is definite chametz and "perhaps they ate it" — doubt does not remove certainty — end. Difficulty: if so, what does the Gemara ask from Rava "middle of courtyard need not check" — perhaps here definite chametz; rather, even definite chametz need not check, as the Gemara: regarding eating there is doubt perhaps they did not eat, but regarding dragging we say "certainly they dragged it." If so, in the mouse case, even if it dragged, it remained in the house; but ravens come from elsewhere and go elsewhere and drag elsewhere — therefore permitted. Perhaps Semak's words "but definite chametz, no" mean we do not rely on "perhaps they ate"; if birds are found in the courtyard, checking is required; but if ravens come from elsewhere here, we say "certainly dragged elsewhere." Also Bach's words regarding a place where they regularly eat — definite chametz — it appears only if they ate close to Pesach; but if they ate long before Pesach and close to Pesach it was guarded that chametz not fall there, no checking, for it is unreasonable that if we saw a mouse drag chametz to a place where chametz was not brought long before Pesach, checking would be required — then all holes where mice are found, even high and low, would require checking, impossible that mice did not drag chametz there; rather there are many such doubts — perhaps dragged elsewhere, perhaps ate, perhaps it became repulsive and unfit for a dog, perhaps was swept, etc. siman 438 — this is not called definite chametz, as written: a wall used with chametz, etc. — these matters are in general, etc. Bach in the name of Rambam and Semag was not precise in their language — it refers to storehouses, not cattle sheds and coops; perhaps all thirty days are called close to Pesach — therefore Maharil wrote not to throw grain to chickens in a damp place thirty days before Pesach — see siman 465.
magen-avraham/7:א: And the rest he nullifies in his heart. Lest it rolled there.
magen-avraham/7:ב: Comes to danger. Although agents of a mitzvah are not harmed where harm is common it is different; Bach asks why not answer perhaps a needle was lost, as in seif 8; one may say here even for definite chametz he need not remove it; and it appears to me there is no proof from this difficulty — one may say it is different: a hole used daily — whence that he would now search for a needle; but in seif 8 it refers to a wall already used and fallen, not now in use — we fear he may now search for a needle already lost; Peri Chadash did not examine the Gemara and wrote on Bach that he did not understand it refers where he did not use it — if he did not use it, obviously no checking, as the Gemara explicitly states — see there; and it appears one must check by daylight all he can, as Rashi's language daf 8 end of 1a.
magen-avraham/8:א: Scorpion danger. It appears specifically where scorpions are found; therefore Rif and Rosh omitted it; perhaps where snakes are found one must check, for their harm is not as certain — see siman 107 seif 3.
magen-avraham/8:ב: After he finishes his checking. For during checking, even searching for a needle, he is an agent of a mitzvah, like one who says "this rock for charity so my sons live" — he is completely righteous even if he intends his benefit (Gemara).
magen-avraham/8:ג: That was lost to him. Beforehand (Rashi) — for during checking he is an agent of a mitzvah and is not harmed even in property.
magen-avraham/8:ד: And this is in general. Even though chametz was used in it, perhaps they will eat it — there are many doubts, as seif 6.
magen-avraham/8:ה: He nullifies in his heart. For Rashi and Ran, nullification is d'rabbanan, since with height of three handbreadths it is as concealed; for Semak, nullification is d'oraisa — so in Magen Avraham, Beit Yosef, siman 438; if he did not nullify until after prohibition time he must open the mound and destroy it since it is not in his power to nullify; but if a large mound fell that he cannot open and it is lost from him and everyone, it is permitted, for we do not call it "yours." Shach wrote: since he did not transgress "it shall not be seen," permitted even in eating after Pesach with no trickery concern since it fell from a collapse — end; requires study (Bach); Rashba responsum 70: Yerushalmi — chametz that fell from collapse is permitted after Pesach, but Rav Hai z"l forbade; so Moreh Nevukhim chapter 3 — see siman 436 seif 1 and siman 448 seif 5.
magen-avraham/9:_: Cellar. Specifically a cellar used for meal needs, without fixed drinking — as seif 3.
magen-avraham/10:_: Require checking. It implies checking as required, i.e. on the night of the 14th.
magen-avraham/11:א: One who sweeps his room. Some practice checking afterward only some rooms — not proper; although Mordechai concludes the reason checking by day does not help is not to divide checking from checking — if so, wherever he did any checking by daylight on the 14th, sweeping suffices; nevertheless he wrote another reason lest something remain in a crevice — then rooms would not be exempt from full checking; therefore full checking is required in all rooms — end Turei Zahav; even if he checked holes and cracks by day he must return at night, as this siman; however if he checked a portico by sunlight he has fulfilled, as Beit Yosef siman 437 in the name of Tosafot; nevertheless at least one room at night so as not to divide checking from checking.
magen-avraham/11:ב: Must sweep. One does not check well without sweeping (Mordechai); therefore they practice taking feathers and sweeping.
magen-avraham/11:ג: That they place in them. One whose practice is not so need not check (Darkei Moshe).
chatam-sofer/1:_: In Mechaber seif 3 "and likewise a barn." NB: storehouse (matban).
chatam-sofer/2:_: There in Magen Avraham s.k. 9 "in a pit." NB: clear (barur).
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 9: "and it is like chametz in a pit." Should read clear (barur).
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Magen Avraham s.k. 5) And oil candle — fearing to put into holes lest oil spill. Nevertheless its law is not like a torch; you might ask wax too — should read as printed. NB: otherwise difficult to include oil with torch in one clause; therefore three laws: torch — even b'dieved must return and check; oil — l'chatchila forbidden by law but b'dieved need not return; fat candle — stringency; practical difference if a place did not accept them — examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 1 — bedikat chametz, etc. NB: if checking on the 13th helps, as Acharonim dispute here — see there; and if one checked on the 13th and nullified, perhaps he need not check again on the 14th if he was careful not to bring chametz in the interim — requires study.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (There seif 11) One who sweeps his room, etc. NB: it appears specifically on the 13th or 12th of Nisan; but if he swept on the 11th, since much time remains until the 14th, he must check on the night of the 14th — examine.
beer-hagolah/1:ג: statement of Rava in the Bavli there
beer-hagolah/2:ב: Tur in the words of his father the Rosh for Ashkenazic custom
beer-hagolah/3:א: Mishnah at the beginning of Pesachim
beer-hagolah/4:ב: Tur and Rabbeinu Yerucham, and likewise the Rosh wrote in a responsum
beer-hagolah/6:ג: Beit Yosef in the name of Semak
beer-hagolah/6:ד: In my humble opinion it appears that here it refers to a guarded courtyard where people dwell, and below it refers to an ownerless place, as mentioned there.
beer-hagolah/9:_: Mishnah at the beginning of Pesachim, and Beit Hillel, as Rav explains in the Gemara 8, and likewise Rambam chapter 2 of Hilchot Chametz u'Matzah
beer-hagolah/10:_: Tur in the name of the Yerushalmi
beer-hagolah/11:_: in the name of R' Avin there
